en.g: Sound more natural by using fillers to buy time like a native speaker.
p: Start an answer: Well, ... Let me think... That's a good question. Hmm, let me see...
Explain or correct yourself: I mean, ... What I'm trying to say is... It's kind of like...
Use them lightly: one or two fillers sound natural, but too many make you sound unsure.
en.q: What's something you find hard to describe in English? Try answering with a filler like Well or Let me think.
en.c: Answer three tricky questions out loud today, starting each one with a different filler: Well, Let me think, I mean.

de.g: Du klingst natürlicher, weil du mit Füllwörtern Zeit gewinnst wie Muttersprachler.

Erklären oder korrigieren: I mean, ... What I'm trying to say is... It's kind of like...
Sparsam einsetzen: Ein oder zwei Füllwörter klingen natürlich, zu viele wirken unsicher.
de.q: Was findest du auf Englisch schwer zu beschreiben? Versuch zu antworten und beginne mit Well oder Let me think.
de.c: Beantworte heute drei knifflige Fragen laut und beginne jede mit einem anderen Füllwort: Well, Let me think, I mean.

es.q: ¿Qué te cuesta describir en inglés? Intenta responder empezando con Well o Let me think.
es.c: Responde hoy en voz alta a tres preguntas difíciles, empezando cada una con una muletilla distinta: Well, Let me think, I mean.

target.gram: Fillers buy time and soften: Well (start or hesitate), I mean (correct or explain), you know (shared idea), Let me think. Use them lightly.

en.t: Softening language: a bit, kind of
en.g: Sound polite and less direct by softening what you say.
p: Soften adjectives: It's a bit expensive. I'm kind of busy. It's sort of complicated.
Use not very + a positive word instead of a strong negative: It wasn't very good is softer than It was terrible.
Soften opinions: I'm not sure that's right. I don't really agree. Maybe we could try another way?
en.q: How would you politely tell a friend that their new haircut isn't your favourite?
en.c: Make three direct sentences softer, e.g. This is boring → This is a bit boring or This isn't very exciting.

de.t: Softening language: a bit, kind of
de.g: Du klingst höflicher und weniger direkt, weil du deine Aussagen abschwächst.
p: Adjektive abschwächen: It's a bit expensive. I'm kind of busy. It's sort of complicated.
Not very + positives Wort statt eines harten Negativs: It wasn't very good klingt sanfter als It was terrible.
Meinungen abschwächen: I'm not sure that's right. I don't really agree. Maybe we could try another way?
de.q: Wie würdest du einem Freund höflich sagen, dass dir seine neue Frisur nicht so gefällt?
de.c: Mach drei direkte Sätze weicher, z. B. This is boring → This is a bit boring oder This isn't very exciting.

es.t: Softening language: a bit, kind of

Usa not very + palabra positiva en lugar de algo negativo fuerte: It wasn't very good suena más suave que It was terrible.
Suaviza opiniones: I'm not sure that's right. I don't really agree. Maybe we could try another way?
es.q: ¿Cómo le dirías con tacto a un amigo que su nuevo corte de pelo no es tu favorito?
es.c: Suaviza tres frases directas, p. ej. This is boring → This is a bit boring o This isn't very exciting.

fr.t: Softening language: a bit, kind of

fr.q: Comment dirais-tu poliment à un ami que sa nouvelle coupe n'est pas ta préférée ?
fr.c: Adoucis trois phrases directes, par ex. This is boring → This is a bit boring ou This isn't very exciting.

it.c: Ammorbidisci tre frasi dirette, ad es. This is boring → This is a bit boring o This isn't very exciting.

en.g: React in conversation to show you're listening and interested.
p: Surprise: Really? No way! You're kidding! Good news: That's amazing! Congratulations! Bad news: Oh no! That's a shame.
Echo questions copy the auxiliary: I've just moved. Have you? / He didn't come. Didn't he? / I can drive. Can you?
Understanding: Oh, I see. That makes sense. Fair enough. Your tone matters as much as the words!
en.q: Tell me something surprising that happened to you. I'll react, and then you react to my story!
en.c: Write three short exchanges: one surprise, one good news and one bad news, each with a reaction and an echo question.

de.g: Du reagierst im Gespräch und zeigst, dass du zuhörst und interessiert bist.
p: Überraschung: Really? No way! You're kidding! Gute Nachricht: That's amazing! Congratulations! Schlechte: Oh no! That's a shame.
Echo-Fragen übernehmen das Hilfsverb: I've just moved. Have you? / He didn't come. Didn't he? / I can drive. Can you?
Verstehen: Oh, I see. That makes sense. Fair enough. Der Tonfall zählt genauso wie die Worte!
de.q: Erzähl mir etwas Überraschendes, das dir passiert ist. Ich reagiere, und dann reagierst du auf meine Geschichte!
de.c: Schreib drei kurze Dialoge: Überraschung, gute und schlechte Nachricht, jeweils mit Reaktion und Echo-Frage.

es.g: Reacciona en la conversación para mostrar que escuchas y te interesa.
p: Sorpresa: Really? No way! You're kidding! Buenas noticias: That's amazing! Congratulations! Malas: Oh no! That's a shame.
Las preguntas eco copian el auxiliar: I've just moved. Have you? / He didn't come. Didn't he? / I can drive. Can you?
Comprensión: Oh, I see. That makes sense. Fair enough. ¡El tono importa tanto como las palabras!
es.q: Cuéntame algo sorprendente que te pasó. Yo reacciono y luego tú reaccionas a mi historia.
es.c: Escribe tres diálogos cortos: sorpresa, buena noticia y mala noticia, cada uno con reacción y pregunta eco.

fr.g: Réagis dans la conversation pour montrer que tu écoutes et que ça t'intéresse.
p: Surprise : Really? No way! You're kidding! Bonne nouvelle : That's amazing! Congratulations! Mauvaise : Oh no! That's a shame.
Les questions écho reprennent l'auxiliaire : I've just moved. Have you? / He didn't come. Didn't he? / I can drive. Can you?
Compréhension : Oh, I see. That makes sense. Fair enough. Le ton compte autant que les mots !
fr.q: Raconte-moi quelque chose de surprenant qui t'est arrivé. Je réagis, puis tu réagis à mon histoire !
fr.c: Écris trois petits échanges : surprise, bonne et mauvaise nouvelle, chacun avec une réaction et une question écho.

it.q: Raccontami qualcosa di sorprendente che ti è successo. Io reagisco e poi tu reagisci alla mia storia!
it.c: Scrivi tre brevi scambi: sorpresa, buona e cattiva notizia, ognuno con una reazione e una domanda eco.

en.g: Keep conversations flowing by asking good follow-up questions.
p: Open questions get longer answers: What happened next? How did you feel? Why was that? What was it like?
What was it like? asks for a description: What was the concert like? It was loud but amazing!
Listen for a detail and ask about it: I went to Japan. → Oh, which city did you visit? Did you try the food?
en.q: Tell me about something you did recently, and then ask me two follow-up questions about my week.
en.c: Today, in a real or imagined chat, ask three follow-up questions starting with What, How and Why.

de.g: Du hältst Gespräche am Laufen, indem du gute Nachfragen stellst.
p: Offene Fragen bringen längere Antworten: What happened next? How did you feel? Why was that? What was it like?
What was it like? fragt nach einer Beschreibung: What was the concert like? It was loud but amazing!
Achte auf ein Detail und frag nach: I went to Japan. → Oh, which city did you visit? Did you try the food?
de.q: Erzähl mir von etwas, das du neulich gemacht hast, und stell mir dann zwei Nachfragen zu meiner Woche.
de.c: Stell heute in einem echten oder ausgedachten Chat drei Nachfragen mit What, How und Why.

es.c: Hoy, en un chat real o imaginario, haz tres preguntas de seguimiento que empiecen por What, How y Why.

fr.c: Aujourd'hui, dans un vrai chat ou un chat imaginaire, pose trois questions de relance avec What, How et Why.

en.g: Enjoy simple English jokes and puns, and understand why they're funny.
p: Many puns use one word with two meanings: Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two tired. (too / two)
Knock-knock jokes play with sounds: Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold! (Let us)
Telling jokes: Have you heard the one about...? Did you get it? I'm just joking! That's so bad it's good!
en.q: Do you know a joke in your language? Could you try to explain it in English?
en.c: Learn one English pun or knock-knock joke by heart and tell it to someone today, then explain why it's funny.

de.g: Du hast Spaß an einfachen englischen Witzen und Wortspielen und verstehst, warum sie lustig sind.
p: Viele Wortspiele nutzen ein Wort mit zwei Bedeutungen: Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two tired. (too / two)
Knock-knock-Witze spielen mit Klängen: Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold! (Let us)
Witze erzählen: Have you heard the one about...? Did you get it? I'm just joking! That's so bad it's good!
de.q: Kennst du einen Witz in deiner Sprache? Könntest du versuchen, ihn auf Englisch zu erklären?
de.c: Lern ein englisches Wortspiel oder einen Knock-knock-Witz auswendig, erzähl ihn heute jemandem und erklär die Pointe.

es.g: Disfruta de chistes y juegos de palabras sencillos en inglés y entiende por qué tienen gracia.
p: Muchos juegos de palabras usan una palabra con dos sentidos: Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two tired. (too / two)
Los chistes knock-knock juegan con sonidos: Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold! (Let us)
Contar chistes: Have you heard the one about...? Did you get it? I'm just joking! That's so bad it's good!
es.q: ¿Conoces algún chiste en tu idioma? ¿Podrías intentar explicarlo en inglés?
es.c: Apréndete un juego de palabras o un chiste knock-knock en inglés, cuéntaselo hoy a alguien y explica la gracia.

fr.g: Amuse-toi avec des blagues et des jeux de mots simples en anglais, et comprends pourquoi ils sont drôles.
p: Beaucoup de jeux de mots utilisent un mot à double sens : Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two tired. (too / two)
Les blagues knock-knock jouent sur les sons : Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold! (Let us)
Raconter une blague : Have you heard the one about...? Did you get it? I'm just joking! That's so bad it's good!
fr.q: Connais-tu une blague dans ta langue ? Pourrais-tu essayer de l'expliquer en anglais ?
fr.c: Apprends par cœur un jeu de mots ou une blague knock-knock en anglais, raconte-la aujourd'hui et explique pourquoi c'est drôle.

it.g: Divertiti con barzellette e giochi di parole semplici in inglese e capisci perché fanno ridere.
p: Molti giochi di parole usano una parola con due significati: Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two tired. (too / two)
Le barzellette knock-knock giocano coi suoni: Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold! (Let us)
Raccontare barzellette: Have you heard the one about...? Did you get it? I'm just joking! That's so bad it's good!
it.q: Conosci una barzelletta nella tua lingua? Proveresti a spiegarla in inglese?
it.c: Impara a memoria un gioco di parole o una barzelletta knock-knock, raccontala oggi a qualcuno e spiega perché fa ridere.

As piadas knock-knock brincam com sons: Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold! (Let us)
Contar piadas: Have you heard the one about...? Did you get it? I'm just joking! That's so bad it's good!
pt.q: Conheces alguma piada na tua língua? Conseguias tentar explicá-la em inglês?
pt.c: Decora um trocadilho ou uma piada knock-knock em inglês, conta-a hoje a alguém e explica porque tem graça.

As piadas knock-knock brincam com sons: Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold! (Let us)

pt_BR.q: Você conhece alguma piada na sua língua? Conseguiria tentar explicá-la em inglês?
pt_BR.c: Decore um trocadilho ou uma piada knock-knock em inglês, conte para alguém hoje e explique por que tem graça.

target.gram: Puns play on two meanings or similar sounds: A book about gravity? It's impossible to put down. (put down = stop reading / drop)

en.g: Use rising and falling intonation in questions, lists and surprise.
p: Yes/no questions usually rise: Do you like coffee? ↗ Wh- questions usually fall: What time is it? ↘
Lists rise, rise, then fall at the end: I need eggs ↗, milk ↗ and bread ↘.
Surprise jumps high: Really?! You did what?! Question tags fall when you're sure, rise when you really ask.
en.q: Say this out loud: Are you hungry? What do you want to eat? Which one goes up and which one goes down?
en.c: Record yourself saying a yes/no question, a wh- question and a list of three things, then check your voice moves.

de.g: Du nutzt steigende und fallende Intonation bei Fragen, Aufzählungen und Überraschung.
p: Ja/Nein-Fragen steigen meist: Do you like coffee? ↗ W-Fragen fallen meist: What time is it? ↘
Aufzählungen steigen, steigen und fallen am Ende: I need eggs ↗, milk ↗ and bread ↘.
Überraschung springt hoch: Really?! You did what?! Question tags fallen, wenn du sicher bist, und steigen bei echten Fragen.
de.q: Sag laut: Are you hungry? What do you want to eat? Welche Frage geht nach oben, welche nach unten?
de.c: Nimm dich auf: eine Ja/Nein-Frage, eine W-Frage und eine Aufzählung mit drei Dingen. Hör, ob deine Stimme sich bewegt.

es.g: Usa la entonación ascendente y descendente en preguntas, listas y sorpresa.
p: Las preguntas de sí/no suelen subir: Do you like coffee? ↗ Las de wh- suelen bajar: What time is it? ↘
Las listas suben, suben y bajan al final: I need eggs ↗, milk ↗ and bread ↘.
La sorpresa sube mucho: Really?! You did what?! Las question tags bajan si estás seguro y suben si preguntas de verdad.
es.q: Dilo en voz alta: Are you hungry? What do you want to eat? ¿Cuál sube y cuál baja?
es.c: Grábate diciendo una pregunta de sí/no, una de wh- y una lista de tres cosas, y comprueba que tu voz se mueve.

fr.g: Utilise l'intonation montante et descendante dans les questions, les listes et la surprise.
p: Les questions fermées montent souvent : Do you like coffee? ↗ Les questions en wh- descendent : What time is it? ↘
Les listes montent, montent puis descendent à la fin : I need eggs ↗, milk ↗ and bread ↘.
La surprise monte haut : Really?! You did what?! Les question tags descendent si tu es sûr, montent si tu demandes vraiment.
fr.q: Dis à voix haute : Are you hungry? What do you want to eat? Laquelle monte et laquelle descend ?
fr.c: Enregistre-toi : une question fermée, une question en wh- et une liste de trois choses. Vérifie que ta voix bouge.

it.g: Usa l'intonazione ascendente e discendente in domande, elenchi e sorpresa.
p: Le domande sì/no di solito salgono: Do you like coffee? ↗ Quelle con wh- di solito scendono: What time is it? ↘
Gli elenchi salgono, salgono e scendono alla fine: I need eggs ↗, milk ↗ and bread ↘.
La sorpresa sale molto: Really?! You did what?! Le question tag scendono se sei sicuro, salgono se chiedi davvero.
it.q: Dillo ad alta voce: Are you hungry? What do you want to eat? Quale sale e quale scende?
it.c: Registrati mentre dici una domanda sì/no, una con wh- e un elenco di tre cose, poi controlla che la voce si muova.

pt.g: Usa a entoação ascendente e descendente em perguntas, listas e surpresa.
p: As perguntas de sim/não costumam subir: Do you like coffee? ↗ As de wh- costumam descer: What time is it? ↘
As listas sobem, sobem e descem no fim: I need eggs ↗, milk ↗ and bread ↘.
A surpresa sobe muito: Really?! You did what?! As question tags descem se tens a certeza e sobem se perguntas mesmo.
pt.q: Diz em voz alta: Are you hungry? What do you want to eat? Qual sobe e qual desce?
pt.c: Grava-te a dizer uma pergunta de sim/não, uma de wh- e uma lista de três coisas, e confirma que a voz se mexe.

pt_BR.g: Use a entonação ascendente e descendente em perguntas, listas e surpresa.
p: Perguntas de sim/não costumam subir: Do you like coffee? ↗ As de wh- costumam descer: What time is it? ↘
Listas sobem, sobem e descem no final: I need eggs ↗, milk ↗ and bread ↘.
A surpresa sobe bastante: Really?! You did what?! As question tags descem se você tem certeza e sobem se pergunta de verdade.
pt_BR.q: Fale em voz alta: Are you hungry? What do you want to eat? Qual sobe e qual desce?
pt_BR.c: Grave-se dizendo uma pergunta de sim/não, uma de wh- e uma lista de três coisas, e confira se a voz se move.

target.gram: Intonation: yes/no questions usually rise, wh- questions usually fall; in lists, voice rises on each item and falls on the last.

en.g: Hear and use weak forms of little words like to, for, can and was in fast speech.
p: In natural speech, small words lose stress and become /ə/: I want to go sounds like I wanna go. A cup of tea → a cuppa tea.
Strong forms come back at the end or for emphasis: Can you swim? Yes, I can! /kæn/. Who's it for? /fɔː/
Stress the important words and let the small ones go quick: I WENT to the SHOP for some BREAD.
en.q: Listen to a short English song or video today. Can you hear the weak forms of to, for or and?
en.c: Practise saying I was going to call you and fish and chips for two quickly, with weak forms, five times each.

de.g: Du hörst und nutzt schwache Formen kleiner Wörter wie to, for, can und was im schnellen Sprechen.
p: Kleine Wörter verlieren die Betonung und werden zu /ə/: I want to go klingt wie I wanna go. A cup of tea → a cuppa tea.
Starke Formen kommen am Ende oder bei Betonung zurück: Can you swim? Yes, I can! /kæn/. Who's it for? /fɔː/
Betone die wichtigen Wörter, die kleinen gehen schnell: I WENT to the SHOP for some BREAD.
de.q: Hör dir heute ein kurzes englisches Lied oder Video an. Erkennst du die schwachen Formen von to, for oder and?
de.c: Sag I was going to call you und fish and chips for two schnell mit schwachen Formen, jeweils fünfmal.

es.g: Escucha y usa las formas débiles de palabras pequeñas como to, for, can y was al hablar rápido.
p: Al hablar, las palabras pequeñas pierden fuerza y suenan /ə/: I want to go suena como I wanna go. A cup of tea → a cuppa tea.
La forma fuerte vuelve al final o al enfatizar: Can you swim? Yes, I can! /kæn/. Who's it for? /fɔː/
Acentúa las palabras importantes y pasa rápido por las pequeñas: I WENT to the SHOP for some BREAD.
es.q: Escucha hoy una canción o un vídeo corto en inglés. ¿Oyes las formas débiles de to, for o and?
es.c: Practica decir rápido I was going to call you y fish and chips for two con formas débiles, cinco veces cada una.

fr.g: Entends et utilise les formes faibles des petits mots comme to, for, can et was à l'oral rapide.
p: À l'oral, les petits mots perdent l'accent et deviennent /ə/ : I want to go sonne comme I wanna go. A cup of tea → a cuppa tea.
La forme forte revient en fin de phrase ou pour insister : Can you swim? Yes, I can! /kæn/. Who's it for? /fɔː/
Accentue les mots importants et passe vite sur les petits : I WENT to the SHOP for some BREAD.
fr.q: Écoute aujourd'hui une chanson ou une courte vidéo en anglais. Entends-tu les formes faibles de to, for ou and ?
fr.c: Entraîne-toi à dire vite I was going to call you et fish and chips for two avec les formes faibles, cinq fois chacune.

it.g: Riconosci e usa le forme deboli di parole piccole come to, for, can e was nel parlato veloce.
p: Nel parlato le parole piccole perdono l'accento e diventano /ə/: I want to go suona come I wanna go. A cup of tea → a cuppa tea.
La forma forte torna alla fine o per enfasi: Can you swim? Yes, I can! /kæn/. Who's it for? /fɔː/
Accentua le parole importanti e passa veloce su quelle piccole: I WENT to the SHOP for some BREAD.
it.q: Ascolta oggi una canzone o un breve video in inglese. Senti le forme deboli di to, for o and?
it.c: Esercitati a dire velocemente I was going to call you e fish and chips for two con le forme deboli, cinque volte ciascuna.

pt.g: Ouve e usa as formas fracas de palavras pequenas como to, for, can e was na fala rápida.

A forma forte volta no fim ou para dar ênfase: Can you swim? Yes, I can! /kæn/. Who's it for? /fɔː/
Acentua as palavras importantes e passa depressa pelas pequenas: I WENT to the SHOP for some BREAD.

pt.c: Pratica dizer depressa I was going to call you e fish and chips for two com formas fracas, cinco vezes cada.

en.g: Learn useful spelling patterns so you make fewer mistakes when writing.
p: Doubling: one short vowel + one consonant → double it: stop → stopped, run → running, big → bigger. But: rain → raining.
Silent e drops before a vowel ending: make → making, hope → hoped. Consonant + y → i: happy → happier, carry → carried.
I before e except after c: believe, friend, piece, but receive, ceiling. Watch out: weird is an exception!
en.q: Which English words do you always find hard to spell? Is there a pattern behind them?
en.c: Add -ing and -ed to five verbs (stop, plan, hope, try, open) and check which spelling rule each one follows.

de.g: Du lernst nützliche Rechtschreibmuster, damit du beim Schreiben weniger Fehler machst.
p: Verdoppeln: kurzer Vokal + ein Konsonant → doppelt: stop → stopped, run → running, big → bigger. Aber: rain → raining.
Stummes e fällt vor Vokal-Endungen weg: make → making, hope → hoped. Konsonant + y → i: happy → happier, carry → carried.
I vor e, außer nach c: believe, friend, piece, aber receive, ceiling. Achtung: weird ist eine Ausnahme!

de.c: Häng -ing und -ed an fünf Verben (stop, plan, hope, try, open) und prüfe, welcher Regel jedes folgt.

p: Doblar: vocal corta + una consonante → se dobla: stop → stopped, run → running, big → bigger. Pero: rain → raining.
La e muda desaparece ante una terminación vocálica: make → making, hope → hoped. Consonante + y → i: happy → happier, carry → carried.
I antes de e, salvo después de c: believe, friend, piece, pero receive, ceiling. Ojo: weird es una excepción.
es.q: ¿Qué palabras en inglés te cuesta siempre escribir? ¿Hay algún patrón detrás?
es.c: Añade -ing y -ed a cinco verbos (stop, plan, hope, try, open) y comprueba qué regla sigue cada uno.

I avant e sauf après c : believe, friend, piece, mais receive, ceiling. Attention : weird est une exception !

pt.g: Aprende padrões de ortografia úteis para dares menos erros ao escrever.

pt.c: Junta -ing e -ed a cinco verbos (stop, plan, hope, try, open) e verifica que regra cada um segue.

en.g: Fix classic B1 mistakes so your English sounds more accurate.
p: Verb errors: I agree (not I am agree). It depends on (not depend of). Listen to music (not listen music).
Word order and objects: Explain it to me (not explain me). Tell me / say to me: She told me, she said to me.
Countable or not: People are (plural). The news is, advice is, information is (uncountable, no -s).
en.q: Which of these mistakes do you make? Is there one that comes from your own language?
en.c: Write five correct sentences using I agree, depends on, explain to me, people are and the news is.

en.g: Celebrate finishing B1 with a recap of linking, register, conditionals and natural conversation.
p: Linking and writing: although, however, because of, so that, as soon as, for example. Paragraphs, reviews and essays.
Register and conditionals: I'm writing to... vs Hi! Quick question. If it rains, we'll... If I were you, I'd...
Natural talk: fillers (Well, I mean), softeners (a bit), reactions (No way!), follow-ups (What was it like?).
